skills.skill: Pairing sums: first and last make the same total
skills.q: Add these numbers. Look for pairs that make the same total. a) 4 + 9 + 14 + 19 + 24 + 29 + 34 + 39 = [ ] b) Add all the whole numbers from 11 to 20.
skills.say: Write the list forwards, then write it again backwards underneath. Add the two numbers that sit on top of each other.
skills.ask: What do you notice about the first and the last? And the second and the second last? How many pairs are there?
skills.listen: "Every pair makes the same total." Check that they count the pairs, not the numbers.

skills.q: Add the numbers. a) 40 + 80 + 120 + 160 + 200 + 240 = [ ] b) Mei saves $5 on day 1, $10 on day 2, $15 on day 3, and so on, up to $50 on day 10. How much has she saved after 10 days?
skills.a: a) 40 + 240 = 280 and there are 3 pairs: 840. b) 5 + 50 = 55 and there are 5 pairs: $275.
skills.say: Try something simpler: do 4 numbers first.
skills.ask: How many pairs? Does it still work if there is an odd number of numbers?
skills.listen: Pairs times total.

skills.q: Each letter stands for one digit. Different letters stand for different digits. Find A, B and C. A = [ ]    B = [ ]    C = [ ]
skills.a: A = 1, B = 9, C = 7 (18 + 79 = 97). Ones: 8 + 9 = 17, so C = 7 and carry 1. Tens: A + 7 + 1 = B, so A + 8 = B. A digit stops at 9, so only A = 1 and B = 9 fit.
skills.say: Start with the ones column, just like the missing-digit sums.
skills.ask: What must 8 + 9 make in the ones? What is the carry? Which letter is it?
skills.listen: The ones column shows C = 7 and a carry. Then test the tens. Ask them to check the whole sum.

skills.skill: Sequences: the gap grows by 1 each time
skills.q: Ali writes a pattern: 6, 7, 9, 12, 16, __, __ a) Write the next two numbers. b) Will 40 be in the pattern?
skills.a: a) 21 and 27 (the gaps are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). b) No: the pattern goes 27, 34, 42 and jumps over 40.
skills.say: This pattern does not add the same number. Make a table and put the gaps in a row of their own.
skills.ask: What are the gaps? How does the gap change? What is the next gap?
skills.listen: "The gap goes up by 1."

skills.skill: Sequences: add the two numbers before
skills.q: Mei writes a pattern: 2, 4, 6, 10, 16, __, __ a) Write the next two numbers. b) What is the 9th number?
skills.say: Try the gap row. Does it look like the numbers?
skills.ask: What is 2 + 4? What is 4 + 6? What would the next number be?
skills.listen: "Add the two numbers before." Ask them to write the whole list to the 9th number.

skills.q: Start at 20. Add 10, then take away 4, then add 10, then take away 4, and keep going. a) Write the first 7 numbers. b) What is the 9th number?
skills.say: Treat each pair of steps as one jump of 6.
skills.ask: What do the numbers in odd places do? In even places?
skills.listen: "Every two steps it goes up 6."

skills.q: Siti counts down: 100, 90, 81, 73, 66, __, __ a) Write the next two numbers. b) What is the gap each time?
skills.a: a) 60 and 55. b) The gaps are 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5: each gap is 1 less than the one before.
skills.say: Draw a table with a row for the gap.
skills.ask: What is the next gap? How do you know?
skills.listen: "The gaps go down 1 each time."

skills.q: Read each story. Draw a bar for each person. a) Ali is 4 years older than his sister. Their ages add up to 20. How old is each? b) Mum is 28 years older than Mei. Mei is 7 now. How old will each be in 5 years?
skills.a: a) Take away the 4 extra years: 16 left, shared equally is 8. Sister 8, Ali 12 (8 + 12 = 20). b) Mei will be 12; Mum is 35 now, so 40 in 5 years. The gap is still 28.
skills.say: For part a, take away the extra years first, then share what is left. The same take-away-the-extra idea as the worksheet.
skills.ask: Which person is older? By how many years? What do you do with the extra 4?
skills.listen: "Both get older at the same speed, so the gap stays." For a), a Guess and check that tests both clues is also fine.

skills.q: Ravi is 9 years old. Mei is 5 years old. a) Ravi will be 12 years old in ___ years. b) Mei will be ___ years old then. c) Ravi was ___ years old when Mei was born.
skills.a: a) 3 years. b) 8 years old. c) 4 years old.
skills.say: Make a small table: year, Ravi, Mei.
skills.ask: What number stays the same in every row?
skills.listen: The gap of 4.

skills.skill: Cubes in the corner of a room
skills.q: Cubes are stacked in the corner of a room, touching both walls. The bottom layer is 3 rows of 3. The next layer is 2 rows of 2. The top layer is 1 cube. a) The bottom layer has ___ cubes. b) The whole stack has ___ cubes. c) ___ cubes touch the left wall.
skills.a: a) 9. b) 14 (9 + 4 + 1). c) 6 (3 in the bottom layer, 2 in the next and 1 on top).
skills.say: Build it layer by layer with cubes, then look at one wall.
skills.ask: Which cubes touch the wall in the bottom layer? In the next layer?
skills.listen: "3, then 2, then 1."

skills.q: A cube corner has layers of 4 by 4, 3 by 3, 2 by 2 and 1 cube. a) How many cubes are there in all? b) How many cubes touch the floor?
skills.say: Make a table: layer, size, cubes.
skills.ask: What pattern do the layer numbers make?
skills.listen: Square numbers: 16, 9, 4, 1.

skills.skill: Picture equations: shapes stand for numbers
skills.q: Each shape stands for a number. The same shape is the same number. a) triangle = [ ]    b) circle = [ ]    c) square = [ ] d) triangle + circle + square = [ ]
skills.a: a) 9 (27 split into 3 equal parts). b) 6 (21 - 9 = 12, shared by 2). c) 7 (13 - 6). d) 22.
skills.say: Find the line that tells you the most. Which shape can you find first?
skills.ask: Which line did you use first and why? How can you check?
skills.listen: Three triangles = 27 is the start. Then use it in line 2.

skills.q: 2 apples weigh the same as 1 melon. 3 melons weigh the same as 1 pumpkin. a) How many apples weigh the same as 1 pumpkin? b) 1 pumpkin and 2 melons weigh the same as how many apples?
skills.a: a) 6 apples (3 melons, each 2 apples). b) 10 apples (6 + 4).
skills.say: Draw it as a chain: apple, melon, pumpkin.
skills.ask: How many apples for one melon? For three melons?
skills.listen: "Multiply along the chain."

skills.q: Today is Thursday. a) What day will it be in 3 weeks? b) What day will it be in 25 days? c) What day will it be in 30 days?
skills.a: a) Thursday (3 weeks is 21 days, 3 full cycles). b) Monday (25 = 3 weeks and 4 days; Thursday + 4 days is Monday). c) Saturday (30 = 4 weeks and 2 days).
skills.say: The week is a repeating pattern of 7. Take out whole weeks first.
skills.ask: How many whole weeks fit into 25 days? How many days are left over?
skills.listen: "Remainder" language: 25 days is 3 weeks and 4 days.

skills.q: A month has 30 days. The 1st of the month is a Tuesday. a) Which dates are Tuesdays? b) What day is the 30th? c) What day is the 1st of next month?
skills.a: a) 1, 8, 15, 22 and 29. b) Wednesday. c) Thursday.
skills.say: Write the dates in rows of 7 under the days of the week.
skills.ask: What do you notice about the Tuesday dates?
skills.listen: They go up by 7.

skills.q: A straight path is 20 m long. A lamp post stands at the start, at the end, and every 5 m in between. a) How many lamp posts are there? b) A fence has 7 posts in a straight line, 3 m apart. How long is the fence?
skills.a: a) 5 posts (4 gaps of 5 m). b) 18 m (6 gaps of 3 m).
skills.say: Draw a dot for each post and a line for each gap.
skills.ask: Are there more posts or more gaps? Why?
skills.listen: "One more post than gaps" in a line.

skills.q: Counting from the front of a queue, Ravi is number 5. Counting from the back, he is number 4. Find the number of children in the queue.
skills.a: 8 children. Ravi is counted twice (5 + 4 = 9), so take 1 away.
skills.say: Draw the queue and mark Ravi.
skills.ask: Who is in front of Ravi? Behind him? Did you count Ravi twice?
skills.listen: "Ravi is counted in both numbers."

skills.skill: Posts and gaps: round a pond
skills.q: 8 lamps stand round a pond, the same distance apart. It is 4 m from one lamp to the next. a) How many gaps are there? b) How long is the path all the way round?
skills.a: a) 8 gaps. b) 32 m.
skills.say: In a ring there is no end post.
skills.ask: Is it the same as a straight path? Why not?
skills.listen: Gaps equal lamps in a ring.

skills.skill: Worst case: how many to be sure?
skills.q: A bag has 6 red counters and 4 blue counters. You take counters out without looking. a) How many must you take to be sure you have 2 red counters? b) How many must you take to be sure you have one counter of each colour?
skills.a: a) 6 (the worst case is 4 blue first, then 2 red). b) 7 (the worst case is all 6 red first, then 1 blue).
skills.say: Be unlucky on purpose. What is the worst that can happen?
skills.ask: What is the unluckiest draw? What counter must come next?
skills.listen: "The unlucky draw is all of the other colour first."

skills.q: A drawer has 4 black socks, 4 white socks and 4 grey socks. You take socks out without looking. a) How many socks must you take to be sure you have a matching pair? b) How many socks must you take to be sure you have 2 black socks?
skills.a: a) 4 (one of each colour is 3 socks; the 4th must match). b) 10 (4 white and 4 grey first, then 2 black).
skills.say: Act it out with coloured counters.
skills.ask: What is the most socks you can take with no pair?
skills.listen: "One of each colour, then one more."
